# piia-engram

Engram is a local-first personal AI identity and memory layer shared across
MCP-compatible coding tools. Its JSON/Markdown data stays on your machine.

Install the package with `pip install piia-engram`, then inspect a dry run:
`engram setup --non-interactive --json`.
One-line install and apply, after inspecting the plan:
`pip install piia-engram && engram setup --non-interactive --apply`.
Use `--clients cursor,codex` to limit clients; `--lang zh|en` defaults to en.
Plan mode writes nothing to the Engram store, home directory or client configs.
Python itself may use the system temporary directory.
Verify with `engram doctor --json`, then restart configured clients.

AI proposes identity and knowledge changes; it cannot approve them through MCP.
Identity changes and high-risk knowledge wait for local owner review: `engram review`.
Strict mode (`ENGRAM_APPROVAL=strict`) queues all knowledge writes for owner review.
Non-interactive setup never imports memories, writes identity/knowledge, or approves proposals.
